reason: Checked every path. sky_row is entered only by JSR, from sky_draw, sky_zero and sky_check (the listing shows no sky_row+N). sky_rn is 1 to 8 for every entry: in sky_hazel's sky_geom, entry 0 is L+1 with L 0-7, the middle rows are 8, and the top row is what is left after taking 8s while it is 9 or more, starting from H-(L+1) >= 15. The split copies rn. So (n-1) EOR 7 = 8-n, and sky_skip, sky_n, s_ptr+1 and Y are unchanged. At exit A = sky_skip and N/Z come from that value, as before. C and V do differ at exit: old C=1 and V=0, new both left as on entry. Nobody reads them. sky_draw's part path does ASL ASL on a value of 7 or less, so C=0 before its ADC. Its whole path reaches next_row's CPX. sky_zero and sky_check do SEC before their SBC. The V tests in render.6502 all follow BIT need,X, and sky_put_on's callers test only C. The CLC hoist is sound. The first entry to .row comes after the new CLC. Every later entry comes from next_row's CPX with BEQ not taken, and X counts up from 1 to sky_nq, so X < sky_nq and C=0. STX, LDA abs,X, ORA #, TAY and LDA abs,Y leave C alone. The OR: sky_s = dm_slot-10 with dm_slot 10 or 11, the only path to sky.6502:248, so it is 0 or 1 and 4*sky_s equals the old 'ORA #4 iff sky_s<>0'. Nothing writes sky_s inside sky_draw, and the interrupt never touches &D2-&E6. The self-modified operand is written and executed in the same call and the same ACCCON state, as the existing cell+1 is. Bytes: sky_row is 3 shorter (22->19 with the SKIP). sky_draw's prologue is +8 and its loop -5, so the net is 0: .row's start shifts but rc_ok and everything after keep their addresses, so no branch timing changes. Stack is unchanged and D is irrelevant. Cycles: sky_row is 29->24 (5 saved a call). Each row of sky_draw saves 6-7, and its prologue costs 13 more once a call.
